alex: quick heads-up — the canary we ran after the driver swap showed a kernel-picker regression on long sequences, looks like a pathing mismatch with the arch-aware rules
chris: ugh, saw that in prod tests? numbers?
maria: yes, on a 1k token trace p95 went from ~92ms to ~158ms after the new driver + autotuner handshake. baseline traces unaffected. reproducer attached. :grimacing:
chris: can you paste the top of the profile? I want to see if the runtime fell back to the slow path (matmul fallback)
maria: pasted below:
```
# perf top (samples)
30%  runtime::kernel_dispatch::slow_matmul
18%  runtime::cache::kv_lookup_lock
12%  runtime::kernel_selector::arch_probe
9%   runtime::batch_scheduler::flush_wait
6%   driver::handshake::model_id_check
```

jia: that slow_matmul spike suggests incorrect kernel choice for the AVX512 path after driver publishes arch hints. maybe the autotuner is ignoring the runtime's seqbin signal?
tim: our new handshake changed the order: driver pushes kernel-profiles then model_metadata. if runtime reads profiles before model id settles we might pick stale kernels for seqlen > 512.
alex: exactly. hypothesize: driver->runtime ordering race leaves kernel_selector with profiles that lack seqlen buckets for new model variant, selector falls back to generic path.
chris: also noticed kv-cache keys include model name + driver-commit but not the model-variant hash. when runtime reloads model with same name but different variant, old entries remain and end up hitting incompatible cache shards. we should never reuse a kv prefix without a variant stamp.
maria: agree. current keyformat: `k:{model}:{shard}:{session}`. proposed: `k:{model}:{variant}:{driver-commit}:{shard}:{session}`. this forces eviction on variant/driver change.
jia: persistence angle: we keep kvstore across restart for warm starts. if we change key format we either need a migration or an invalidation sweep. migration is heavy. invalidation is easier: emit a `lease`/`epoch` token on driver <-> runtime handshake and check: if epoch != cached_epoch then drop namespace.
tim: sketch of handshake patch I ran locally:
```
driver -> runtime: {model, variant, arch_profiles, epoch: 42}
runtime: load profiles, set local_epoch=42, accept requests
on restart: if incoming.epoch != local_epoch -> mark namespace stale -> async sweep
```

alex: that avoids big migrations. downside: on small multi-tenant drivers it may flush some good cache, but still better than silent wrong-kernel hits.
chris: for rollout plan: patch selector to prefer explicit seqlen buckets if available, keep fallback. then add epoch check and keyformat change (non-destructive). Canary with 5% traffic for 2 hours, then 25% for 6 hours, monitor p95 and kernel dispatch histogram.
maria: added a little diagnostic we can include in the canary headers to assert kernel_choice provenance:
```
X-Profiler: kernel_choice=arch_bucket(v512),source=selector_v2,epoch=42
```
so we can correlate request length -> chosen path.
perf-bot: [perf-ci] baseline: p95=92ms, canary=154ms, kernel_dispatch=slow_matmul:+68% (see link: https://perf.company/internal/3050000000)
alex: good. action items: (1) chris/jia update key format + epoch handshake PR, (2) tim add ordering guard in driver publish to ensure profiles appear after model id settled, (3) maria add header diagnostics and canary dashboard. Aim to gate canary until epoch invalidation is in.
chris: will open PR today, include migration-safe flag and runtime config toggle.
jia: will add epoch check to kv namespace logic; default to enabled in next minor.
maria: I'll schedule the canary and patch the dashboard. tagging @sre for on-call awareness. :thumbsup:
tim: thanks — will also add a quick test in the selector unit tests to simulate profile-order race.
alex: awesome. if anyone sees new regressions after the PRs land ping here. closing thread for now. :raised_hands:
